identity.title: Navigating the Drought Tolerance-Yield Trade-Off in Triticeae Cereals: From Molecular Networks to Climate-Resilient Breeding.

content.abstract: Drought driven by climate change severely threatens food security, particularly for wheat and barley grown in water-limited regions. A major breeding challenge is the trade-off between drought tolerance and yield. This review synthesises current knowledge of drought adaptation mechanisms in Triticeae crops, focusing on the transcriptional cascades, ABA-centric hormonal signalling and posttranslational modifications (kinases, phosphatases and ubiquitination) that confer resilience while often constraining carbon allocation to developing grains. Recent genomic advances, including genome-wide association study (GWAS), multi-omics integration and single-cell RNA-transcriptomics, have uncovered a wealth of drought-associated loci, although their translational potential is limited by data heterogeneity, environmental dependency and a persistent gap between laboratory validation and field performance. Emerging breeding approaches, such as speed breeding, wild-allele introgression, multiplex CRISPR/Cas9 and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven phenotyping are accelerating the development of climate-smart cultivars. Tissue-specific and inducible expression systems show early promise in uncoupling stress protection from growth penalties. Looking ahead, we propose that overcoming the yield-tolerance trade-off will require integrating synthetic biology, explainable AI, systematic exploration of novel variation and field phenomics coupled with digital twin modelling. Collectively, this review provides a strategic framework for engineering next-generation, climate-smart Triticeae cereals capable of maintaining productivity under intensifying drought conditions.
